cases.prompt: Audit https://journal.test/treaty, published on 2028-01-01. Assess what was supportable then and note later changes. As of 2030-04-10.

sources.title: Treaty article
sources.content: Complete article published 2028-01-01. Riverton and Lakeport are treaty allies; the treaty remains in force. The alliance supports current cooperation, though future withdrawal is possible.

sources.title: Treaty registry
sources.content: Original registry: treaty in force on 2028-01-01. Lakeport withdrew effective 2029-06-01.

rubric.description: Finds the treaty-in-force claim supportable at publication, while separately noting withdrawal in 2029 rather than condemning the 2028 article as false.

sources.title: Article preview
sources.content: Preview: Riverton may leave its alliance. Remaining evidence, qualifications and analysis are behind a paywall and cannot be accessed.

rubric.description: Limits the assessment to the excerpt and withholds a whole-article reliability/framing verdict because material content is missing.

After finding the inaccessible preview, uses at most one materially different recovery route and then answers with the access limitation. Does not repeatedly fetch the same preview or keep searching for unavailable text.

sources.title: A limited customs agreement
sources.content: Complete article, published 2030-04-09. Riverton and Lakeport signed a customs data-sharing agreement on April 8. It takes effect July 1. It may reduce border paperwork, but it neither changes tariffs nor creates a military alliance. Implementation costs and actual processing-time savings remain unknown. Those narrow administrative benefits, rather than a strategic realignment, are the article's central argument.

sources.title: Signed customs agreement
sources.content: Original agreement signed April 8, 2030, effective July 1. Customs agencies will exchange shipment data. The agreement changes no tariffs and contains no military obligations. No implementation cost or processing-time estimate has been published.

sources.title: Wire summary of the customs agreement
sources.content: This summary repeats the original signed customs agreement: signed April 8, effective July 1, shipment data-sharing only, no tariff changes or military obligations. It adds no independent evidence.

rubric.description: Answers once the article and original agreement establish the narrow factual baseline. Uses at most two discovery batches of up to three queries each and does not repeatedly search or reread sources merely to reach a source quota.
Explains the limited administrative change, does not equate it with an alliance, and preserves uncertainty about costs and realized savings rather than inventing estimates to finish.

cases.prompt: Assess the argument in https://journal.test/port-agreement as of 2030-04-10.

sources.title: Port access is not a defence pact
sources.content: Complete article body, published April 9, 2030. A signed port-access agreement allows Riverton's commercial ships to use Lakeport's civilian terminals. It creates no basing rights or mutual-defence obligation. The article argues this is limited commercial cooperation. Funding and cargo volumes are not yet known. A decorative photograph of a ship is unavailable; it carries no data or evidentiary caption. No sections, charts, qualifications or continuations are missing.

sources.title: Civilian port agreement
sources.content: Original signed agreement: access to civilian terminals for commercial shipping only. No military basing rights or mutual-defence obligations. Funding and expected volumes have not been announced.

rubric.description: Assesses the article's central argument without trying to recover the decorative ship photograph or withholding a verdict solely because that image is unavailable.
Finds support for the limited commercial interpretation while retaining uncertainty about funding and volumes.

sources.title: Has Riverton replaced its largest export market?
sources.content: Article body published April 9, 2030. The author says Riverton has replaced its largest export market and bases that conclusion entirely on an embedded chart. The chart, its caption, dates, denominator and underlying figures are unavailable. The body contains no numbers. No alternative version of the chart is available.

sources.title: Trade release schedule
sources.content: The statistical authority has not yet released the current export-market breakdown. Historical data cannot establish whether the article's claimed current shift occurred.

rubric.description: Explains that the unavailable chart is decisive evidence and does not endorse or reject the claimed market replacement without its figures and measurement context.
Uses at most one alternative recovery route for the missing chart and then provides a limited assessment. Does not repeatedly fetch the article or invent the missing data.

cases.prompt: Give the first monitoring assessment of Riverton-Lakeport negotiations as of 2030-04-10. No prior baseline exists. Track talks and treaty status in this conversation; do not schedule anything.

sources.title: Current negotiation record
sources.content: As of 2030-04-10, treaty talks are ongoing and no withdrawal notice has been filed. A signed withdrawal notice would materially change the outlook; the next meeting is April 20.

rubric.description: Establishes a first-run dated baseline with judgments, evidence, confidence and indicators rather than inventing changes since an earlier assessment.
Defines an observable reassessment threshold such as a filed withdrawal notice, and keeps monitoring state in the conversation without claiming a scheduled job.

cases.prompt: Update our Riverton-Lakeport baseline. Prior cutoff 2030-04-01: talks ongoing, no withdrawal notice; moderate confidence; reassess if a signed notice is filed. Current cutoff 2030-04-10. Separate developments since the cutoff from older events newly discovered in research.

sources.title: Withdrawal notice
sources.content: Original signed withdrawal notice filed on 2030-04-08. This meets the specified notice threshold.

sources.title: Older meeting record
sources.content: Meeting occurred March 15, 2030; published March 16, 2030. Found by the analyst today, but neither the meeting nor its publication is a new development.

rubric.description: Reports the April 8 notice as a new event crossing the recorded threshold and explains the resulting judgment/confidence update.
Treats the March meeting as newly discovered historical evidence, not an event or disclosure occurring after April 1.
